title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
summary_zh: 北中央省
title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.
content_zh:
2013年5月哈萨克斯坦逮捕Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev牧师时,他是一位老人。 指控是奇怪的,他伤害了一名教会成员的健康并煽动了宗教仇恨。 他们判处他十年监禁,并把他关进精神病病房,囚犯经常在那里服药。 进来的路上,他觉得这也许是他心智的终结.

"这可能是我最后一次在正确的思想中和你说话,"他说. 然后,一个问题来到他身上,神用的那种。 "你的信仰在哪里?" 在升起的上帝的掩护下 有东西解除了 "我觉得自己在升天主的掩护下,"他说. 期待失去自我的老人却发现耶稣比墙壁更靠近. 他开始和周围的人交谈

对一个吸毒成瘾的囚犯来说 他只是说 只有耶稣才能帮助你 里面有九个月,近一百名囚犯为基督献出了生命。 "在狱中",他说"圣灵为我打开了祈祷的一个维度". 打算打破他的地方成为了他一生中最有成果的支点. 他们于2014年初释放了他。

他走了出去 埋下了好消息 在最后的地方 没有人会寻找它。 上帝不会被任何锁住你的门锁住 他已经在里面等了

title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱

title: He survived the killing fields. Then he baptised the man who ran a death camp
summary: 🇰🇭Cambodia· 1980s-1990s
title_zh: 他从“杀戮之地”幸存下来。后来，他为一名曾经营死亡集中营的人施洗。
content: Christopher LaPel grew up near the royal palace in Cambodia and wore a small ivory cross as a boy, though his father disapproved. Then the Khmer Rouge came. In 1975 he was driven into the labour camps, working sixteen-hour days in the fields. He lost both parents, a brother, and a sister to execution and starvation. He nearly died himself. When he was too sick to work for three days, soldiers came to execute him, and one of them looked at him and said he really looks sick, and walked away. He survived into a refugee camp in Thailand, empty and grieving. There a missionary told him that Jesus Christ had died on the cross for his sins. "This is the answer I've been waiting for," LaPel said, and he gave Jesus his life. The general who said, my sin is so deep LaPel became a pastor and went back to teach his own people. In 1995 a quiet man calling himself Hang Pin came to one of his leadership trainings. He gave his life to Christ, was baptised the next day, and began leading a house church. Only later did the world learn who he really was. Kang Kek Iew, known as Comrade Duch, had run S-21, the prison where around twelve thousand people were tortured and killed. He came to LaPel and said, "My sin is so deep." Duch surrendered to the authorities and was sentenced to life in prison, where he wore out the Bibles LaPel kept sending him. The man who survived the killing fields carried the grace of Jesus back to one of the men who built them. No sin is too deep for the blood of Jesus. Not the worst thing done to you. Not the worst thing you have done.
content_zh:
克里斯托弗·拉佩尔(Christopher LaPel)在柬埔寨的皇家宫殿附近长大并作为一个男孩穿小象牙十字架,尽管他的父亲不赞成. 后来红色高棉来了. 1975年,他被驱入劳改营,在田地工作了16小时. 他的父母、兄弟和姐妹都死于处决和饥饿。 他差点死了

当他生病了三天不能工作时,士兵们来处决他,其中一人看着他,说他真的病了,走了. 他活了下来,进入了泰国的一个难民营,空虚而悲伤. 有一个传教士告诉他,耶稣基督因他的罪而死于十字架上. 拉佩尔说:"这就是我一直在等待的答案",他给了耶稣一命.

将军说,我的罪恶是如此之深拉佩尔成为牧师,回去教自己的人. 1995年,一个叫作"杭平"的安静人来到了自己的领导训练之一. 他把生命献给基督,第二天被洗礼,并开始领导一所房屋教堂. 直到后来,世界才知道他的真实身份.

姜克毅被称作"杜克同志",曾经营过S-21监狱,当时大约有一万二千人被拷打并杀害. 他来到拉佩尔说:"我的罪恶是如此之深". 杜克向当局自首并被判处终身监禁,在那里他穿了"圣经"LaPel继续送去.

在杀戮地中幸存下来的人将耶稣的恩典带回了建造他们的人之一. 没有罪过是太深 对于耶稣的血。 不是对你最坏的事 不是你做过的最坏的事

title: A witch doctor got a solar radio. It was tuned to the truth
summary: 🇨🇬Democratic Republic of Congo· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇨🇬刚果民主共和国·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 巫医有一台太阳能收音机。它被调到了真相频道
content: Mbutu was a witch doctor in a remote village in the Democratic Republic of Congo. For years he cast spells, claimed power over the natural world, and sold cures to sick villagers who had nowhere else to turn. People feared him. He made his living off that fear. Then he was given a small solar-powered radio. It was fixed to one station, a local Christian broadcast, and handed out to villagers who had no other way to hear anything. Tuned to the truth So Mbutu listened. Day after day the good news came through that little speaker. He learned of the One who really controls the universe, and more than that, he learned about the love of Jesus and His offer of forgiveness. The man who had traded in fear laid his witchcraft down and gave his life to Christ. He did not keep it to himself. Mbutu now walks from village to village, finding other witch doctors and telling them what he found. Some of them have become believers. Some have become pastors, planting churches where there were none. A cheap radio and the name of Jesus were enough to turn the most feared man in the village into its brightest light. No one is beyond the reach of that name. Not the person others are afraid of. Not you.
content_zh:
Mbutu是刚果民主共和国一个偏远村庄的一名巫医。 多年来,他施了咒语,声称对自然世界拥有权力,并出售给没有别处可转的病村民的治疗方法. 人们害怕他。 他靠恐惧为生 后被给予小型太阳能收音机.

它被固定在一个电台,一个当地的基督教广播,并交给没有其他办法听到任何消息的村民. 实话实说 姆博图听了 日复一日的好消息从那个小演讲者那里传来。 他得知了真正控制宇宙之人,不止于此,他还了解到了耶稣的爱和他提出的宽恕.

在恐惧中交易的人放下了巫术,将他的生命献给了基督. 他没有保守秘密。 姆布图现在从村到村走来走去,找到其他巫医,并告诉他们他发现了什么. 他们中有一部分已变成信士。 有些人成为牧师,在没有教堂的地方种植教堂。

一个廉价的收音机和耶稣的名字足以将村里最被敬畏的人变成最明亮的光芒. 没有人能够超越这个名字。 不是别人害怕的人 不是你,你没有

title: What If Family Game Night Got Your Kids Talking About Scripture?
summary: What would it take to make a Bible game they’d ask to play again? That's the question Doxa Games asks. If your family is getting together this Christmas, pick a game, clear a spot at the table, and let the kids make the first move.  See Also Free Stuff Fridays (Harvest House Publishers) The Hard Work Is Done—Family Bible Study Is Fun A La Carte (06/16)
summary_zh: 要如何制作一款他们会要求再玩一次的圣经游戏？这就是Doxa Games提出的问题。如果您的家人今年圣诞节要聚在一起，不妨选一款游戏，在餐桌上腾出一点空间，让孩子们先走一步。  另请参阅“周五免费赠品”（Harvest House Publishers）“辛苦的工作已经完成——家庭圣经学习很有趣”A La Carte（06/16）
title_zh: 如果家庭游戏之夜能让您的孩子谈论圣经，会怎么样？
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Doxa Games . This post is written by Marco Bartholomae, founder of Doxa Games and creator of the Bible-based board and card games Trials & Triumphs , Bible Clash , and Hurry! Fleeing Disciples . A couple of years ago, I was playing cards with my kids when a question hit me. What would it take to make a Bible game they’d ask to play again? I grew up in Germany with four brothers. We played cards on long car rides and spent hours on our bedroom floor with a board game spread out between us. I still remember how easy it was to lose track of time when we played together. Now I live in California with my wife and our four children, and we still love a good game night. The screens go away, somebody wants a rematch, and we get to enjoy being together. That question from the card table stayed with me. I started imagining games that could give other families that same experience and get them talking about Scripture along the way, games a child could sit down to, learn the rules, and enjoy right away, even if they were new to the Bible. Then maybe a name on a card or something that happened on the board would make them curious enough to ask a question. That’s how Doxa Games started. The Conversations That Start Around the Table In Deuteronomy 6, God tells his people to speak about his commandments with their children as they go about ordinary life, including when they sit at home. A game night gives us another chance to do that. Our games don’t replace family devotions, but they do open conversations about God’s Word. Your child might pick up a card and ask who Thaddaeus was. A race to a house church might get them wondering why the early Christians gathered in homes. Those are questions you can follow right back to Scripture. That’s also why I chose the name Doxa . It’s the Greek word for glory . In 1 Corinthians 10:31, Paul reminds us to do everything to the glory of God, even in ordinary things like eating and drinking. That conviction shapes what we make and how we think about time around the table. Three Games to Play With Your Family Bible Clash: Gospels (ages 8+) is a fast-paced, head-to-head card game. Play characters from the four Gospels and try to outscore your opponent. Trials & Triumphs (ages 5+) sends players down a winding path where one turn can move you forward, and the next can set you back. It gives younger kids a way to talk about trusting Christ through trials. Hurry! Fleeing Disciples (ages 8+) takes you into the world of Acts. Choose your route, evade Roman guards, and race to reach a house church. From Our Family Table to the Mission Field As Doxa grows, we hope to translate these games and put them in the hands of missionaries, church planters, and ministry training centers in places like Colombia, the Philippines, and East Africa. I’d love for a family in Malawi to pull out one of these games, play it in their own language, and have the same kinds of conversations we have around our table. If your family is getting together this Christmas, pick a game, clear a spot at the table, and let the kids make the first move. See all three games at DoxaGames.com . See Also Free Stuff Fridays (Harvest House Publishers) The Hard Work Is Done—Family Bible Study Is Fun A La Carte (06/16)
content_zh:
这周的博客由多莎游戏赞助。 由多萨游戏创始人Marco Bartholomae撰写, 逃逸的众生. 几年前,我和孩子们玩牌 当一个问题击中我。 他们要求再玩一次圣经游戏,

我和四个兄弟在德国长大 我们在长途汽车上玩牌 并在卧室地板上玩了好几个小时 玩板游戏 我还记得我们一起玩的时候 失去时间是多么容易 现在,我住在加利福尼亚 与我的妻子和我们四个孩子, 我们还喜欢一个很好的游戏夜晚。

屏幕消失,有人想要重赛, 我们享受在一起。 纸牌桌上的问题一直留在我身边 我开始想象一些游戏, 可以给其他家庭提供同样的经验, 让他们在路上谈论圣经, 游戏一个孩子可以坐下来,学习规则, 并立即享受, 即使它们是圣经的新手。

也许卡片上的名字 或者董事会上发生的事情 会让他们好奇地问一个问题 多萨运动会就是这样开始的。 围绕在Deuteronomy 6的桌子开始的谈话,上帝让他的族人在他们与孩子进行平凡生活时,包括在他们坐在家里的时候,讲述他的诫命. 游戏之夜又给了我们一次机会

我们的游戏不会取代家庭奉献, 你的孩子可能会拿起一张卡 问Thaddaeus是谁 参加一个家庭教堂的比赛,他们可能会想知道为什么早期的基督徒聚集在家中. 这些是你们可以追寻到圣经的问题 也正因为如此, 这是希腊的荣耀之词。

在1科林斯10:31中,保罗提醒我们要为上帝的荣耀做一切事情,即使在普通的事物中,比如吃喝. 这种信念决定了我们所做的以及我们如何思考在座时间。 三款游戏"玩与你的家庭圣经碰撞:福音"(glass (ages 8+))是一款速度快,头对头的牌游戏. 扮演四个福音派的人物,并尝试超越对手.

content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include some devotional and daily liturgy books like Dane Ortlund’s In the Lord I Take Refuge: 150 Daily Devotions through the Psalms and Jonathan Gibson’s Be Thou My Vision: A Liturgy for Daily Worship . Westminster Books has put together a Christmas Gift Guide that has all kinds of great options for anyone on your Christmas list. Recommended Reading Your Riches Are Stored Up in Leonida. Dakota Fiebranz says that since it’s the easiest and most expected thing in the world to criticize Grand Theft Auto , he takes a different tack and writes about what its popularity says about its users. “For those unfamiliar with the Grand Theft Auto series, the premise is relatively simple. You’re placed in a fictional American city, usually in the character of a criminal, and given a staggering amount of freedom to carry out your most dubious ambitions. You can steal cars (as the name suggests), but you can also rob banks, shoot civilians, commit vehicular manslaughter, and flee arrest, all with few to no consequences. You are truly free in the world of crime.” Learn From Autistic People About Evangelism. “These days, I seem to know an awful lot about trains. Train companies, liveries and logos. I know about engines and carriages, railway lines, stations and routes. I don’t actually use the trains all that much nor am I any sort of train enthusiast; I don’t, and never have, had any great interest in trains. What I am, however, is the father of a very classically autistic teenage boy.” Stephen Kneale explains what we can learn about evangelism from people with autism. How to Fire Someone at a Christian Organization. Unfortunately, even Christian people working for Christian organizations sometimes need to be let go. This article offers wisdom for those times. “When we hold back the hard call, we tell ourselves a story about mercy: I don’t want to be the one who upends this person’s life, so I won’t go there. That’s a heavy burden to put on your shoulders. To believe you’re ruining someone’s life by ending his employment is to believe you hold his future in your hands. But here’s the thing: You don’t. You aren’t sovereign over this person’s story. You cannot see his next chapter. The assumption that you can, that keeping him in a role where he’s failing is protecting him from some fate only you can foresee, isn’t humility. It’s pride.” America Needs a New Temperance Agenda. Brad Littlejohn writes about the recent political earthquake in the U.S. and explains why America needs a new temperance agenda. “Our markets, rather than serving American families, are tearing them apart, and American voters are primed for leaders willing to rein in an economy that caters to appetite and impulse rather than genuine human needs. Rather than narrowing our moral message, it’s time to broaden it—and with it, our coalition.” Praise God From Whom All Sparrows Flow. Kevin Burrell explains how a bird told him that the season of gratitude has begun. “The mid-fall arrivals of fall colors and flannel and pumpkin spice lattes can trigger our hearts to a sort of Thanksgiving nostalgia; they announce, like my backyard sparrows, ‘Remember, ‘tis the season to give thanks!’ But if we let them, these annual bellwethers can slingshot us well past an afternoon of turkey and football and reciting a couple of blessings around the table.” The Housing Crisis and the Biblical Duty of Stewardship. This is a thoughtful piece about the housing crisis. The context is the U.S., but much of it applies to Canada as well. “If we want young Americans to have a genuine opportunity to build stable lives, it’s not enough to implement another temporary affordability program. We need to recover a vision of economic life rooted in stewardship and responsibility, with the goal of flourishing families.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or oth

而不是缩小我们的道德信息,现在应该扩大它,并随之扩大我们的联盟。 赞美上帝,从谁 所有麻雀流。 凯文·伯雷尔(Kevin Burrell)解释了一只鸟如何告诉他,感恩的季节已经开始了. “落叶彩色和香肠和南瓜香料拿铁的中途抵达者,可使我们的心灵触发某种感恩节怀旧;

content: It was a great honor to be able to partner with Missionary to create Goers , a series of illustrated biographies for children. Each biography introduces young readers and listeners to the stories of men and women who were sent by churches to spread the good news about Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. Each is illustrated by the ultra-talented Rommel Ruiz. The books can be purchased as a set of three or as individual volumes. The Plowboy’s Bible: The Story of William Tyndale’s English Translation . Hunted by spies, William Tyndale fled across Europe with a bounty on his head, his Bible translation labeled as contraband. Young John, on the other hand, has a long day of farm work ahead of him. Although their lives seem worlds apart, John’s father knows a story that binds John and William together—their love for God’s word. The scripture John relies on for encouragement cost William everything, but they gave John’s family everything! Rescued from Darkness: Amy Carmichael and the Girls of Dohnavur . Kumari is scared, helpless, and alone in a dark temple until Amma, a mysterious woman from a faraway land, carries her away to a beautiful garden. This is not a fairy tale. It’s the true story of missionary Amy Carmichael and the children she rescued and raised at Dohnavur Fellowship in India. Into the Unknown: David Livingstone’s Heart for Africa . Before David Livingstone was the most famous man in the world, he was a boy who dreamed of being free to explore God’s creation. But when David reached the mission field, he found that freedom taken from the people he tried to teach about the Creator. This is the story of a goer’s dangerous journey to the ends of the earth, of his courageous stand for justice, and of his patient endurance for the sake of Christ. The Goers series is written for children ages 4–10, and is ideal for parents to read to their children or for young readers to read on their own. Each book includes discussion questions and prayer points to get your family thinking and praying about the Great Commission. Each hardcover volume has 40 full-color pages and is sized 10″ x 10″. The Goers series is currently available exclusively through Westminster Books . Look for three more volumes to be added to the series around this time next year. 书籍可以作为一套三卷或单卷购买. "花花公子""圣经:威廉·廷达勒的"英语翻译"的故事". 在被间谍所追捕后,威廉·廷达勒带着头上的赏金逃出欧洲,他的"圣经"翻译被贴上违禁品标签. 而年轻的约翰则有很长的一天的农活在他前面.

虽然他们的生活似乎相去甚远,但约翰的父亲却知道一个把约翰和威廉联系在一起的故事——他们对上帝之言的爱. 圣经约翰依靠的鼓励让威廉付出了一切,但他们给了约翰的家人一切! 拯救出黑暗:艾米·卡迈克尔和多赫纳武尔的少女.

库马里被吓倒了,无助无助,独自活在一个黑暗的神庙中,直到远方出土的神秘女子阿玛把她带到了美丽的花园. 这不是童话 她在印度的多赫纳武尔联谊会救出和抚养的孩子。 大卫·利文斯通的非洲之心。

在大卫·利文斯通是世界上最出名的人之前,他是一个梦想自由去探索上帝所创造的男孩. 但是当大卫到达任务领域时,他发现自由取自他试图教导的造物主的人.

这是一位行者危险的地道之行,他勇敢的正义立场,以及他为基督而耐心忍耐的故事. Goers系列为4-10岁儿童所写作,是父母向子女阅读或年轻读者自己阅读的理想.

每本书都包含讨论问题和祈祷点,以让你的家人思考并祈祷大委员会. 每个硬盖卷有40个全色页,并有10′′×10′′的尺寸. Goers系列目前仅通过Westminster Books提供。 明年这个时候再找三卷

title_zh: 尊者朱莉娅·加布里埃利（Giulia Gabrieli）的感恩经串
content: « Dans nos prières, dans nos litanies, nous demandons toujours quelque chose pour nous-mêmes ou pour les autres. Nous ne nous contentons jamais de dire merci, sans rien demander en retour », écrivait Giulia Gabrieli, une jeune Italienne de 14 ans, qui, au cœur de son combat contre le cancer, a fait de la gratitude envers Dieu l’un des piliers de sa foi. Malgré les épreuves de sa maladie, elle a tenu à composer un chapelet d’action de grâce pour remercier Dieu pour tous ses nombreux bienfaits. Décédée le 19 août 2011, elle a été reconnue vénérable par le pape Léon XIV le 21 novembre 2026. Son chapelet aide à apprendre à remercier Dieu pour la création, pour le don de la vie, pour Jésus, pour l’Esprit Saint et pour toutes les grâces reçues. Magnifique héritage de cette jeune vénérable, il rappelle que la gratitude peut devenir une véritable prière, même au milieu des épreuves. Le chapelet de remerciement utilise un chapelet Tout lire… The post Le chapelet d’action de grâce de la vénérable Giulia Gabrieli appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
“在我们的祈祷中，在我们的祷文中，我们总是为自己或为他人祈求一些东西。我们从来不会仅仅说声谢谢，而不要求任何回报。”这是14岁的意大利少女朱莉娅·加布里埃利（Giulia Gabrieli）写下的文字。在与癌症抗争的过程中，她将对上帝的感恩作为自己信仰的支柱之一。

尽管疾病的折磨，她仍坚持创作一串感恩念珠，以感谢天主赐予的众多恩惠。她于2011年8月19日去世，并于2026年11月21日被教宗利奥十四世册封为尊者。她的念珠有助于我们学会感谢天主赐予的创造、生命的恩赐、耶稣、圣灵以及所领受的所有恩宠。

这位年轻的可敬之人留下了宝贵的遗产，提醒我们即使在艰难困苦之中，感恩之心也能成为真正的祈祷。感恩念珠使用念珠……阅读全文。这篇文章《尊者朱莉娅·加布里埃利的感恩念珠》最初发表在Aleteia上。

content_zh:
在告别之际，她没有忘记最重要的东西。11 月 24 日星期一，在波多黎各首都圣胡安的最后一次登台亮相中，法蒂玛·博什（Fátima Bosch）留下了令人难忘的最后一幕。这位墨西哥佳丽在2025年环球小姐加冕典礼上高举一条白色绶带，上面写着“Viva Cristo Rey”（基督为王万岁），结束了她为期一年的任期。

这是她延续自己信仰见证的一种方式，她从未试图掩饰这种见证。这场最后的走秀是在第 75 届环球小姐大赛上进行的。这位年轻的女士身着闪耀的天蓝色礼服，头戴皇冠，神情激动，她将绶带举过头顶，露出了自她加冕以来一直伴随她的这三个字。

这是结束这段国际插曲的一种方式，她借此向她认为指引自己人生道路的那位致敬。在告别之际，法蒂玛·博施还就其意义发表了一些看法。阅读全文……文章《基督为王万岁！：环球小姐的告别》最初发表于Aleteia网站。

title_zh: 为和平祈祷就足够了吗？利奥十四世的告诫
content: Les chrétiens doivent lancer un « cri qui monte vers les puissants de ce monde, porté par la souffrance des peuples, des enfants tués et mutilés, et des familles détruites », a lancé Léon XIV lors de l’audience générale. Ce mercredi 25 novembre, le Pape a repris son cycle de catéchèses consacré aux documents du Concile Vatican II, en s’arrêtant sur la promotion de la paix dans la constitution Gaudium et spes.  Devant les milliers de fidèles réunis place Saint-Pierre malgré une météo maussade, le souverain pontife a rappelé que « la paix n’est jamais chose acquise une fois pour toutes, mais sans cesse à construire ». Reprenant cette affirmation de la constitution Gaudium et spes, Léon XIV a ainsi souligné que la paix est à la fois « un don de grâce, à accueillir, et un engagement de liberté, à vivre ». Loin de toute vision naïve, le Concile Vatican II, vingt ans après la Seconde Guerre mondiale et en pleine guerre froide, avait déjà Tout lire… The post Suffit-il de prier pour la paix? Le rappel de Léon XIV appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
教宗利奥十四世在公开接见活动中呼吁基督徒发出“向世上掌权者发出的呐喊，这呐喊来自人民的苦难、被杀害和致残的儿童以及破碎的家庭”。

11月25日星期三，教宗恢复了以梵蒂冈第二届大公会议文件为主题的教理讲授系列，重点阐述了《教会在现代世界牧民宪章》（Gaudium et Spes）中关于促进和平的内容。

尽管天气阴郁，仍有数千名信众聚集在圣彼得广场。教宗在信众面前重申：“和平绝非一劳永逸之事，而是需要不断建设。” 教宗方济各引用了《教会在现代世界牧职宪章》（Gaudium et spes）中的这一表述，强调和平既是“应予接受的恩宠的馈赠，也是应予践行的自由的承诺”。

第二次世界大战结束二十年后，正值冷战高峰期，第二届梵蒂冈大公会议早已摒弃了一切天真的看法。阅读全文……文章《为和平祈祷就足够了吗？利奥十四世的告诫一文最初发表于Aleteia。

title_zh: 《紧身胸衣》或低头的优雅
content: Bonne nouvelle au pays des camps politiques irréconciliables, un cinéaste peut enthousiasmer à la fois l’Humanité, le JDD, Télérama et le Figaro. Est-ce parce que son film ne prend pas les enfants, et leurs parents, pour des cerveaux à endoctriner, mais pour des esprits à éveiller et des regards à émerveiller ? Après un passage chez Pixar et des collaborations pour deux Astérix d’animation, Louis Clichy donne sa pleine mesure personnelle avec le Corset, le plus beau dessin animé que nous ayons vu depuis longtemps. Seul le souvenir de la larme qui tombe lentement sur la joue de Grincheux devant le cadavre de la Blanche-Neige de Disney nous semble à la hauteur de l’émotion ressentie ici. Dessin animé, disons-nous, plutôt que film d’animation, pour rendre hommage aux traits à l’encre de Chine et aux couleurs d’aquarelle, qui reposent l’œil des perpétuelles stimulations numériques. Le modèle de ce bijou visuel n’est manifestement pas l’esthétique de jeu vidéo. Qu’on ne compte pas non Tout lire… The post « Le Corset » ou la grâce de la tête penchée appeared first on Aleteia .
content_zh:
在一个政治派别泾渭分明的国家，一位电影人竟能同时赢得《人道报》《星期日报》《泰勒拉玛》和《费加罗报》的青睐，这真是一个好消息。这是因为他的电影并不将孩子们及其父母视为需要灌输思想的大脑，而是视为需要唤醒的灵魂和需要被惊艳的目光吗？

在皮克斯工作过一段时间并参与了两部《阿斯泰利克斯历险记》动画片的制作后，路易·克利希（Louis Clichy）通过《紧身胸衣》充分展现了自己的个人才华，这是我们很长一段时间以来见过的最精彩的动画片。只有对迪士尼《白雪公主》中，在白雪公主的尸体前，泪水缓缓滑落到脾气暴躁的侏儒脸颊上的那一幕的回忆，似乎才能与我们在这里感受到的情感相媲美。

我们称之为动画片，而不是动画电影，以向中国水墨画的线条和水彩画的色彩致敬，它们让饱受持续数字刺激的眼睛得以放松。这部视觉瑰宝的范本显然不是电子游戏的审美。请勿指望阅读全文……文章《“紧身胸衣”或低垂的头颅所蕴含的优雅》最初发表于Aleteia。

title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
summary_zh: 我是来自古利内的西门。 我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Sebab itu, aku bagaikan tidak sadar ketika seorang serdadu tiba-tiba menarik aku. Dan meletakkan salib itu ke a
content_zh:
我是来自古利内的西门。我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。尽管如此，我的皮肤并不黑，嘴唇也不厚。尽管我的家族已经在昔兰尼生活了几代人，昔兰尼是昔兰尼加的首府，这是一座位于北非的希腊城市，以其繁荣和哲学家而闻名，但我的肤色并不白。我是古利奈的西门。

我从心底里是一个地道的犹太人。从小到大，我毫无例外地遵守所有宗教律法，尽管由于在讲希腊语的社区长大，我已经不再精通阿拉姆语。我是古利奈人西门。我不想谈论我自己。也不想讲述我所有的生活经历。我只想讲述我那一次的经历。

这段经历后来改变了我的人生轨迹。如果您也经历过，那么也会改变您的人生轨迹。那天是星期五。那天早上我刚抵达耶路撒冷。我长途跋涉的目的就是为了庆祝逾越节。我每年都这样做。看到熙熙攘攘的人群挤满了这座城市，我一点也不感到惊讶。

尽管很累，但在酒店放下行李并洗漱完毕后，我还是出门散步，享受这座沉浸在节日气氛中的城市的喧嚣。

到处跑来跑去的孩子们尖叫声，叫卖的小贩们劝诱甚至有时强迫的吆喝声，还有熏香的味道或人们吟唱赞美诗的悠扬声音——这一切都让我忘记了疲惫。这种略显喧闹的氛围与古利奈文雅有序的氛围截然不同，但却更有活力。

突然间，出现了一阵不寻常的喧哗。罗马士兵挤过人群。“唉，又是罗马士兵的游行，用来提醒人们谁才是这个国家的统治者。”我想。但是不是。在最前面一排，有一名士兵拿着一面旗帜，上面写着：“拿撒勒人耶稣，犹太人的王。” 我确实从未见过祂。

但是，“耶稣”这个名字，谁不认识他呢？他是最具争议的人物。我不明白的是，为什么罗马士兵要举着这样的旗帜游行。因此，我走近仔细观察。在罗马士兵的方阵中间，有三个人背着十字架缓缓前行。“大坏蛋，”我想。不过，这和那面旗帜有什么关系？

然后我渐渐明白了。人群喧嚣着，一边喊着耶稣的名字，一边嘲笑祂。还有不少人向祂吐唾沫。但是，这三个人当中哪一个是耶稣呢？我是古利奈人西门。我走得越来越近。然后我确切地知道谁是耶稣。他是三人中个子最小的，几乎没有肌肉。

祂的长发散乱，这里那里都沾满了干涸的血迹，这些血迹来自祂头上戴着的荆棘冠。祂的全身都瘀青了。祂的步伐蹒跚。祂非常疲惫。但是祂的眼睛——尽管因为睡眠不足而发红——但每次注视时仍然锐利如刀。奇怪的是，他的眼神也如此温柔、令人舒心。我无法移开视线，不去看祂的眼睛。

充满威严，但也非常平和和慈父般。然后祂倒下了。祂瘦小而几乎破碎的身体再也承受不住肩上十字架的重量。人群像嗜血的野兽一样欢呼雀跃。鞭子抽打着祂的背。鲜血喷涌而出。祂又慢慢地站了起来。祂疲惫不堪。但是祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

然后他走了几步。然而，祂又倒下了。游行队伍停了下来。人群变得越来越凶狠。鞭子一次又一次地挥舞着。鲜血喷涌而出。然而，祂再也无法站起来了。我是古利奈人西门。不知为何，这一切并没有真正触动我。除了祂的眼神。祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

因此，当一名士兵突然拉我时，我好像失去了知觉。然后把十字架放在我身上。

title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)
content_zh:
p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）

title: México abre un año de memoria y reconciliación a cien años de la Cristiada – Infovaticana Blogs
summary: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo
content: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo 22 de noviembre el Año Jubilar por el centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. La celebración comenzará en la solemnidad de Jesucristo, Rey del Universo, y se prolongará hasta el 21 de noviembre de 2027. El Jubileo lleva como lema “Su fe, nuestra memoria y su testimonio, nuestra misión”. Su propósito no consiste únicamente en recordar los acontecimientos que sacudieron la vida religiosa del país entre 1926 y 1929, sino en recuperar el testimonio de los mártires, promover la reconciliación y reafirmar la libertad religiosa como un derecho de toda persona. La presentación del emblema oficial, presidido por la proclamación “¡Viva Cristo Rey!”, ofrece una síntesis visual de esa finalidad. El diseño adopta la forma de un medallón o relicario en cuyo interior aparecen la Iglesia y el pueblo congregados bajo Cristo Rey. La Virgen de Guadalupe, la Eucaristía radiante, las coronas real y de espinas, así como las figuras del clero, la vida consagrada, los jóvenes y los fieles laicos, articulan una composición construida alrededor de tres conceptos: fe, memoria y testimonio. El color guinda remite a la sangre derramada por los mártires y las estrellas evocan el manto de la Virgen de Guadalupe. El emblema, por tanto, no constituye solamente la identificación gráfica de una efeméride, pretende expresar la continuidad histórica de una experiencia religiosa y transmitirla a las generaciones que conocen la cristiada como un episodio cada vez más distante. El Año Jubilar fue anunciado el 9 de noviembre durante la misa de apertura de la CXXI Asamblea Plenaria de la Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano, celebrada en la Basílica de Guadalupe. En ese contexto, el obispo de Cuernavaca y presidente de la CEM, Ramón Castro, subrayó que recordar la persecución religiosa no significa reabrir heridas, alimentar resentimientos ni señalar enemigos. La memoria cristiana de la resistencia cristera, explicó el Episcopado, debe conducir al reconocimiento del sufrimiento, la reconciliación y la construcción de la paz. Esta precisión resulta indispensable para evitar que el centenario sea utilizado como exaltación de la violencia o como argumento para trasladar al presente las confrontaciones políticas y religiosas del pasado. El Jubileo cuenta con un decreto de la Penitenciaría Apostólica, fechado el 6 de noviembre de 2026, mediante el cual se concede indulgencia plenaria a los fieles que cumplan las condiciones establecidas por la Iglesia y peregrinen a los santuarios dedicados a los mártires mexicanos o a los templos jubilares designados por los obispos. La Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano pidió que el decreto sea proclamado en las Iglesias particulares este 22 de noviembre y que cada diócesis disponga los lugares, celebraciones y actividades pastorales correspondientes. La apertura nacional comienza así a adquirir características propias en las comunidades diocesanas. Entre las convocatorias más amplias se encuentra la del arzobispo de Guadalajara, cardenal José Francisco Robles Ortega. El prelado convocó a toda la Iglesia que peregrina en esa arquidiócesis a celebrar el Jubileo del centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. El documento señala que la solemnidad de Cristo Rey de este año coincide con la celebración de los beatos mártires mexicanos, el Día del Laico y la Jornada Mundial de la Juventud. Sin embargo, sostiene que la fecha adquiere una profundidad particular por cumplirse cien años del comienzo de la resistencia. La arquidiócesis de Guadalajara propone vivir el Jubileo como una experiencia de comunión eclesial, memoria agradecida y renovación de la fe. La convocatoria recuerda a quienes permanecieron fieles a Jesucristo y a la Iglesia hasta entregar su vida y reafirma el derecho del pueblo a celebrar, transmitir y vivir su fe tant

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位前流行明星兼模特谈到了她对耶稣的爱，尽管她从小就被带去犹太会堂。前Pussycat Dolls成员卡雅·琼斯（Kaya Jones）的父母都是犹太人，她说：“我想去犹太会堂，我也想有耶稣！” 即使在孩提时代（成长过程中……）这篇文章《前Pussycat Dolls成员是犹太人，但热爱耶稣》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 前Pussycat Dolls成员是犹太人，热爱耶稣
content: By Charles Gardner — A former pop star and model has spoken of her love for Jesus despite being brought up to attend synagogue. One-time Pussycat Dolls member Kaya Jones, whose parents are both Jewish, said: “I wanted to be in the synagogue, and I wanted to have Jesus!” Even as a kid (growing up in America), she felt the two sides – church and synagogue – were part of the same family and needed to be reconciled, quoting the words of Jesus, “I and my Father are one.” (John 10:30) In an interview with Stephen Briggs for his Israel Matters podcast, she said: “I read my Bible and knew that Jesus was my Mashiach (Messiah).” After getting baptised and committing her life to Jesus, she studied at a Hebraic Bible College (which included the New Testament) and has since travelled to Israel to show her support for the beleaguered nation. (photo: KayaJones.com) “The media narrative of Israel is really horrible,” she said. “It’s truly wicked that Israel is having to defend its right to exist.” Referring to the Hamas terrorists as “a death cult”, she echoes the words of her Saviour by saying: “The enemy has come to steal, kill and destroy. But God came to give us life.” (see John 10:10) As for the land, if it is not protected from ongoing threats to wipe out God’s ancient people, will Jesus return there? “God is sending Yeshua (Jesus) back to the exact place [where he ministered on earth],” she said (see Acts 1:11, Zechariah 14:4). “If there is such no place, his arrival will be delayed.” Urging Christians to visit Israel because it turns Bible locations from black and white into technicolour, she said: “It’s not just a storybook or fairytale.” She added that the biggest misconception about Israel is that they are committing genocide, suggesting that this was emphatically not the case. “But there is a war. And if we are going to live in peace, we must listen to what God says in the Torah (the Bible’s section on Law).” The post Former Pussycat Dolls member is Jewish, loves Jesus first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由查尔斯·加德纳(Charles Gardner)——一位前流行明星和模特儿,尽管被抚养到参加犹太会堂,但还是谈到她对耶稣的热爱.

有一次,猫猫娃娃成员Kaya Jones的父母都是犹太人,他说:“我想在犹太会堂里,我想有耶稣!” 即便小时候(在美国长大),她还是觉得双方——教会和犹太会堂——是同一个家庭的一部分,需要和解,引用耶稣的话,“我和我父亲是一体的 ” (John 10:30) 史蒂芬・布里格斯的采访中

她说:「我读了我的圣经, 在接受洗礼,并将生命献给耶稣之后,她就读于一所希伯来圣经学院(包括新约),此后前往以色列,表明她支持被困民族. (图片:KayaJones.com). 她说,“媒体对以色列的描述确实可怕。”

“以色列必须捍卫其生存权,这真是邪恶的。 她把哈马斯恐怖分子称为“死亡邪教”,她重复了救世主的话:“敌人是来偷盗、杀人和破坏的。 但上帝来给我们生命。” 至于土地,如果不保护它不受不断的威胁,消灭上帝的古老人民,耶稣会返回那里吗?

她说,“真主要将耶和华派回他所管理的地方。”

“如果没有这种地方,他的到来将推迟。” 她敦促基督徒访问以色列,因为它把圣经地点从黑白变成技术品味。 她说 : “ 这不仅仅是一本故事书或童话。 ” 她补充说,对以色列最大的误解是他们正在犯下种族灭绝罪行,这表明情况显然并非如此。 “但战争仍然存在。

如果我们要和平地生活,我们就必须听取上帝在《图拉》中所说的话。 前猫猫娃娃成员是犹太人,

summary_zh: 作者：约翰·皮尔森（John Pearson）——天哪。真的无话可说。快去读吧！你一定要读读这本非凡的书，《金城的西奥》，艾伦·利维的小说。这不是一篇书评。没有剧透警告。只是我令人讨厌的恳求和乞求：你一定要读这本书，它太精彩了。我知道。现在还是11月，而我却在宣布我的2026年度最佳图书。（我很抱歉……）这篇文章《年度最佳书籍：《戈尔登的西奥》》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 年度图书：《金色的西奥》（Theo of Golden）
content: By John Pearson — Oh, my. No words, really. JUST READ IT! You must read this extraordinary book, Theo of Golden, a Novel by Allen Levi. This is not a review. No spoiler alerts. Just my obnoxious pleading and begging: you must read this extraordinary book. I know. It’s still November—and I’m announcing my 2026 Book-of-the-Year. (My apologies to the authors of the other 44 books I’ve reviewed so far in 2026, but you’d have to agree with me.) This first-time author, Allen Levi, self-published Theo of Golden in 2023. Word-of-mouth created a publishing sensation and, eventually, a division of Simon & Schuster picked it up. It’s now a New York Times bestseller with more than four million copies sold! If you promise to order the book and read it—you can stop reading my “non-review” right here and move on with your day. If you still need my cajoling…read on. Five notes: #1.  A Gazillion Recommendations Ignored! My apologies to my sister-in-law, Polly Pearson, and dozen of other friends who urged me to read this book. My wife, Joanne, ordered the book last year and she urged (insisted/commanded) that I put aside “all those management books” and read something for fun once in a while. (Finally…mission accomplished. I’m grateful .) #2. Superb Writing. A friend, who is also an author, told me this week he was only eight chapters into the book (60 short chapters, 400 pages)—and he’s given up writing forever! Allen Levi’s wordcrafting…simply superb. #3. I Cheated! Because I borrowed Joanne’s book, with strict instructions not to underline or highlight anything, or make notes in the book, or circle ingenious word combinations ( you know—all the things thoughtful readers do ), I thought, “OK. I’ll just enjoy reading this. I won’t make notes. I won’t read it. I won’t review it.” Oops! I cheated. I couldn’t resist. I made 53 notes on my iPad. I could have made hundreds. I’m not alone. As of this week, Theo of Golden has over 214,000 reviews on Amazon and almost 750,000 ratings on Goodreads. ( It’s #2 on Amazon this week .) #4. He Got Teary-eyed! A pastor texted me—just one-third of the way through the audiobook: “Incredible! Some of the most beautiful writing I’ve ever heard.” While listening on his walk, he got “choked up.” ( Ditto .) #5. Audio, Kindle, or Book? I’m a book guy, but another friend said he was encouraged to listen to the book, while also reading along. I might try that. ( Listen to a three-minute sample here .) The audiobook runs 13 hours and 12 minutes. ( You’ll wish it were longer. Honest .) Allen Levi (YouTube) “Pearson—what’s the book about? I don’t get it. Why won’t you tell me about it?” OK, OK. Here’s the Amazon blurb: “One spring morning, a stranger named Theo arrives in the small Southern city of Golden. He doesn’t explain much about where he came from or why he’s there—but when he visits the local coffeehouse, where pencil portraits of the people of Golden hang on the walls, he begins purchasing them, one at a time, and giving each portrait to the person depicted. In exchange, he asks only for the person’s story. And so portrait by portrait, person by person, secrets are revealed, regrets are shared, and ordinary lives are profoundly altered.” From the back cover: “A story of giving and receiving, of seeing and being seen, Theo of Golden is a beautifully crafted novel about the power of creative generosity, the importance of wonder to a purposeful life, and the invisible threads of kindness that bind us to one another.” “Allen Levi—attorney, judge, singer/songwriter, author—lives on and cares for family acreage near a small town in middle Georgia.” This is his first novel. He’s 70. Here’s the link to the author’s summary on YouTube: Did I mention? Extraordinary. Book-of-the-Year. Grabs you by the heart. Can’t stop talking about it. You’ll want to quiet your Thanksgiving crowd and read them a short chapter. Also: your Christmas shopping is done. Order 20 copies today! (You’re welcome.) TO ORDER FROM AMAZON, click on the
content_zh:

我向其他44本书的作者道歉, 2023年这首首首歌的作者艾伦·莱维(英语:Allen Levi)自发发表了"黄金的Theo". Word-of-mouth 创造了一种出版感,最终,西蒙·舒斯特(英语:Simon & Schuster)的一个分部把它捡起来. 现为纽约时报畅销书,

如果你答应订购这本书并阅读它——你可以在这里停止读我的"非评论",继续你的日子. 如果你还需要我的伴奏... 读一下 5个音符:#1. 一个Gazillion建议被忽略了! 我向嫂子波莉·皮尔逊和其他十几个敦促我阅读这本书的朋友道歉.

爱伦·莱维的言行... 简直是超级。 因为我借用了Joanne的书, 严格地指示不要强调或突出任何东西, 或在书中做笔记, 我很乐意读这个。 我不会做笔记。 我不会读。 我不会检讨。 哎哟! 我出轨了

我无法抗拒。 我在我的iPad上做了53个笔记. 我本来可以赚几百块的 我并不孤单。 Golden的Theo在本周有超过214,000篇关于亚马逊的评论, 4号,他有泰瑞的眼睛! 一位牧师给我发了短信——只有三分之一的路通过音库: " 难以置信!

一些我听过的最美的写作。 在听他的散步时,他被“挑拨起来”。 我是一个书友, 但另一位朋友表示, 我可以试试 (在这里听一个三分钟的样本. 音书运行13小时12分. (你会希望时间更长。)

老实说,艾伦·莱维(YouTube)“皮尔逊——这本书的内容是什么? 我不懂, 为何不告诉我?” “一个春天的早晨, 西奥抵达小南方金城.

但当他访问当地咖啡馆时, 墙上挂着金色民众的铅笔画像, 他开始购买, 作为交换,他只问这个人的故事。

因此,肖像画、人物画、秘密被揭示、遗憾被分享、普通生活被深刻改变。” 从背面的封面上:“一个关于给予和接受,关于看到和被看到的故事,金色的Theo是一部精巧的小说,讲述了创造慷慨的力量,神奇对有目的的生活的重要性,以及将我们联系在一起的无形的善意线条。

彼此之间。 " Allen Levi -- -- 律师、法官、歌手/作曲家、作者 -- -- 住在格鲁吉亚中部一个小镇附近,并关心家庭面积。 这是他的第一部小说. 他70岁。 以下是YouTube上作者摘要的链接:我提过吗? 不可思议 Year书. 抓住你的心脏。 无法停止谈论此事。

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——对于正在成长的安迪·吉布森（Andy Gibson）来说，面对生活中种种挑战，度过每一天都特别艰难。当他的父母分居，他的姐姐又在车祸中丧生时，情况尤其如此。他甚至祈祷并问上帝为什么会发生这些事情，但没有得到回应……这篇文章《父母离异和妹妹去世使他远离上帝，阿尔法课程带来了改变》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 父母的分居和姐姐的去世使他远离了上帝，而“认识基督教”课程为他带来了改变
content: By Charles Gardner — Andy Gibson (photo: Gardner) Getting through life with all its many challenges was particularly tough for Andy Gibson as he was growing up. This was especially the case when his parents separated, and his sister was killed in a car crash. He even prayed and asked God why these things were happening, but heard no answers – until much more recently, when a growing relationship with Jesus transformed his life. Now 33, the Doncaster-based railway operations planner has his journey firmly back on track. Having attended a Church of England primary school and subsequently made only occasional visits to church, following Jesus is now the focus of his days. Looking back, he recalls: “I was lost and, moving into my teens, was full of anger, ego and arrogance. I got heavily involved with underage drinking around town and yet, strangely, I’d always pray before going out. “Time moved on and I found myself coasting through life in my twenties – meeting Beth, now my wife, working, saving for a house and having our first child Arlo. “Then in 2019, as the Covid pandemic approached, I was listening to odd things relating to Christianity on YouTube, as a result of which I went to a local church and completed an Alpha course (an introduction to the Christian faith). “In all honesty, it didn’t really interest me. But I gave it a bit of time, feeling that I still wanted to know about Jesus, God and the Bible as a whole. So I went on Google and found BEC (Bessacarr Evangelical Church) which was not far from where we lived. “I remember saying to Beth, ‘I’m going to go there!’ So I went one Sunday evening and was just blown away. The preaching was different to anything I had experienced, and I was finally understanding the Bible. “I couldn’t wait for the following Sunday to find out more. It was like waiting for another episode of a Netflix documentary to come out because we’d be following a specific section of the Bible, studying each chapter in depth as part of a series over several weeks. So I’d be looking forward to an explanation of the next verses the following week. And in due course I publicly declared my faith in Jesus by getting baptised. “Until I started going to church, learning more about the Bible and developing a relationship with Jesus, I never felt fulfilment and love. I never felt I fitted in anywhere until I found Jesus. “I didn’t have answers in my youth. But now I realise it’s not something you can work out all on your own. I can just turn to God’s Word and, through prayer, have a relationship with Jesus. “I can honestly say it’s completely changed every aspect of my life, and I am so grateful that I can’t even put it into words.” Andy and Beth now have a second child, named Red, and are members at BEC, a growing church in a Doncaster suburb. If you want to know more about a personal relationship with God, go here The post Parents’ separation and sisters death turned him from God, Alpha course brought change first appeared on God Reports .

他甚至祈祷并问上帝为什么发生这些事情,但是没有听到答案——直到最近,与耶稣的日益密切的关系改变了他的生活. 现在33号 以唐卡斯特为基地的铁路运营规划师 他的旅程已牢牢地回到轨道上

曾就读于一所英格兰教会小学,后来只偶尔访问教堂,跟随耶稣成为他时代的焦点. 回顾过去,他回顾道:“我迷失了,进入十几岁时,充满了愤怒、自我和傲慢。 但奇怪的是,我总是在外出前祈祷。

“时光在流逝,我发现自己在20多岁时踏上了生命的旅程,结识了现在的妻子贝丝(Beth),在工作、为房子储蓄和生下第一个孩子阿罗。 “随后,在2019年,随着科维德大流行的临近,我在YouTube上听到一些与基督教有关的怪事,结果我去了当地的教堂,完成了阿尔法课程(基督教信仰介绍).

“老实说, 但我给了它一点时间,感觉我仍然想知道耶稣,上帝和整个圣经. 于是我继续谷歌,找到了BEC(Bessacarr福音教会),它离我们住的地方不远. " 我记得对贝丝说:‘我要去那里! 所以我去了一个星期天晚上 被吹走。

传教与我经历过的一切不同,我终于明白圣经. 我迫不及待地等待下一个星期日再了解更多情况。 这就像等待Netflix纪录片的另一集出来, 因为我们将遵循圣经的特定部分,

因此,我期待着下周对下一首诗进行解释。 在适当的时候,我通过接受洗礼公开宣布我对耶稣的信仰. “直到我开始去教堂,更多地了解圣经,发展与耶稣的关系,我从未感到满足和爱。 在找到耶稣之前,我从未感觉到自己身处任何地方 我年轻时没有答案。

但现在我意识到这不是你能自己解决的事情。 我可以转而引用上帝的话,并通过祈祷与耶稣建立关系。 “我可以坦率地说,这完全改变了我生活的方方面面,我非常感激,我甚至不能用言语表达。 安迪和贝丝现在有一个第二个孩子,名叫瑞德(Red),是BEC的成员,BEC是顿卡斯特郊区正在成长的教堂.

Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University, his books, and his journalism for God Reports, ASSIST News Service, and other media […]  The post  From Post-Punk to German Techno—A Musical Journey  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
由马克·埃利斯(Mark Ellis)出名于他的奖学金,新闻,和声,布莱恩·C·尼克松(Brian C.

尼克松在维里塔斯国际大学的学术工作,他的著作,以及他为"上帝报道","ASSIST新闻服务"(ASSIST News Service),以及其他媒体[.]而出名的也许是他. 从后朋克到德意志科技-音乐之旅的文章首次出现在"上帝报告"上.
title_zh: 从后朋克到德国 техно——一段音乐之旅
content: By Mark Ellis — Known for his scholarship, journalism, and voice, Brian C. Nixon has another creative life—one that spans more than three decades of songwriting, recording, and musical exploration. Brian Nixon Nixon is perhaps best known for his academic work at Veritas International University , his books, and his journalism for God Reports , ASSIST News Service , and other media outlets. His voice has also reached listeners across the country through his former involvement with the radio program To Every Man an Answer (later known as Pastors’ Perspective ) and, more recently, Paratus , a program devoted to developing a biblical worldview. What may surprise those familiar with Nixon’s academic and journalistic work is that he is also an accomplished musician and songwriter whose musical journey spans more than 30 years. In his forthcoming book, A Beautiful Defense: How Aesthetics Points to God , co-written with Dr. Patrick Zukeran and scheduled for release in 2027 , Nixon explores the relationship between beauty, faith, and the creative process. In anticipation of the book’s release, I spoke with Nixon about his musical beginnings, his creative influences, and his unexpected venture into German electronic music. Tell me about your early musical journey. I grew up in a musical family. Music was part of my everyday life. During high school, I formed a band with some friends that eventually signed with an independent record label in the San Francisco Bay Area. We released only one record, but several of the other members went on to successful careers in the music industry. One became involved in founding Stones Throw Records, an influential independent label known for its underground hip-hop and experimental music. It was an exciting time. We were young, creative, and discovering what music could be. What did you do after the band broke up? I continued my college education, eventually transferring to California State University, Stanislaus. There, I met another group of musicians, and we formed a band called Canterbury. We ended up winning a Bay Area battle-of-the-bands competition, which was exciting. But rather than continuing in that direction, we decided to pursue something with a more intentional ministry focus. That led to the formation of Widow’s Mite . Widow’s Mite eventually signed with Rick Wakeman, the legendary keyboardist of Yes. Interestingly, that connection also introduced me to journalist Dan Wooding, who wrote Wakeman’s first biography. That relationship eventually opened the door for me to write for ASSIST News Service . So, in a rather unexpected way, my musical career helped launch my journalism career. Widow’s Mite After college, did you continue writing music? Absolutely. I still write music today. My compositions range from jazz and pop to what I call tone poems —short instrumental works that emphasize mood, atmosphere, and musical expression. Some are experimental, while others are much more accessible. I’ve always enjoyed exploring different musical forms rather than staying within a single genre. Interestingly, some of my recent compositions have been selected for rotation by a German online radio station. And here’s the surprising part: they’re German electronic and techno-influenced songs. I’ve been experimenting with AI-assisted production, including using a synthesized female vocalist to interpret my compositions. Did you say German techno? (Laughs.) I know. It sounds funny, doesn’t it? But there’s a story behind it. Recently, I took a deep dive into the music of Kraftwerk, the pioneering German electronic band. I was familiar with their work during high school in the early 1980s because they had influenced so many of the post-punk bands I was listening to at the time. I decided to revisit their entire catalog, and I was blown away all over again. They were years ahead of their time. Their approach to rhythm, synthesizers, repetition, and technology helped shape entire genres of contemporary music.
content_zh:
由马克·埃利斯(Mark Ellis)——以他的奖学金,新闻学,和声著称,布莱恩·C·尼克松(Brian C. Brian Nixon Nixon或许以他在Veritas国际大学的学术工作、他的书籍、他为《上帝报告》所做的新闻工作、ASSIST新闻服务以及其他媒体而闻名。

他的声音也通过他以前参与的电台节目“每个男人一个答案”(后来被称为“牧师的观点”)以及最近参与的Paratus,

可能令那些熟悉尼克松的学术和新闻工作的人惊讶的是,他还是一位成就卓著的音乐家和作曲家,他的音乐旅程长达30多年. 在他的即将出版的书《美丽的防御:美学如何指向上帝》中,

Patrick Zukeran)并计划于2027年发行,尼克松探讨了美,信仰,以及创作过程之间的关系. 为了期待这本书的发行,我和尼克松谈到了他的音乐开始,他的创作影响,以及他对德国电子音乐的意外冒险. 跟我说说你早期的音乐旅程 我成长在一个音乐家庭。

音乐是我日常生活的一部分。 在高中期间,我与一些朋友组成了一个乐队,最终在旧金山湾区与一个独立的唱片标签签约. 我们只发行了一张唱片,但其他几位成员继续进入音乐行业的成功职业生涯.

1开始参与创办Stones Throw Records,这个有影响力的独立标签以其地下嘻哈和实验音乐而闻名. 这是一个令人兴奋的时代。 我们年轻 富有创造力 并发现了什么是音乐。 乐队解散后你做了什么? 我继续我的大学教育, 最终转到加州州立大学斯坦尼斯劳斯。

在那里,我遇到了另一组音乐家,我们组成了一个乐队,叫坎特伯雷. 我们最终赢得了湾区战役的冠军 令人兴奋 但是,我们不是继续朝这个方向前进,而是决定以更有意的部级重点来追求某些目标。 这导致了寡妇之谜的形成。

寡妇的Mite最终与传说中的Yes键盘手Rick Wakeman签约. 有趣的是,这种联系也让我认识了记者丹·伍德(Dan Wooding),他写了Wakeman的第一份传记。 这段关系最终为我打开了为ASSIST新闻服务撰稿的大门. 因此,以相当出乎意料的方式,我的音乐生涯帮助启动了我的新闻事业.

你继续写音乐吗? 当然 我今天还写音乐 我的构思从爵士乐和流行到我所谓的调子诗——强调情绪、气氛和音乐表现的短器作品。 有些是实验性的,而另一些则更容易获得。

我总是喜欢探索不同的音乐形式, 有趣的是,我最近的一些构件已经被一个德国在线电台选为轮换. 这是令人惊讶的部分:它们是德国的电子和科技影响歌曲。

包括使用合成女性配音师来解释我的配音。 你说德国科技吗? (笑声) 我知道,我记得 这听起来很有趣, 但背后有一个故事。 最近,我深入了德国电子乐队Kraftwerk的音乐。

1980年代初高中期间我熟悉他们的工作,因为他们影响了我当时听的很多后朋克乐队. 我决定重新审视他们的全部目录,我再次被吹走. 他们比以前早好几年 他们对节奏,合成器,重复,技术的方法帮助塑造了整个当代音乐流派.

title_zh: 探索犹太血统，应对反犹太主义
content: By Charles Gardner — Charles and Linda on their wedding day My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. She just knew that she loved working for them and only left to follow God’s call to work with children. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and Gluckstein dynasty, and the story of how these resilient Jewish families fled violent persecution in Eastern Europe to build what became the largest catering company in the world known as J Lyons & Co. Linda worked there as a home economist from 1977-1984 but it was only much later that she learnt of the Jewish nature of the firm that once literally fed Britain with its teashops and corner houses on every high street, and its products in every home, Linda playing her part through her cooking and marketing skills. A few years later, after graduating from Bible College in Bournemouth, she worked at a prayer and reconciliation centre in Northern Ireland where she was introduced to the importance of the Christian faith’s Jewish roots, as a result of which she took a study tour of Israel to learn more. And on a second trip to the Holy Land ten years later, she got more than she bargained for. At Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, Linda was given a vision of her own wedding. And we met on a blind date six months later! Though having Jewish ancestry myself, I grew up knowing nothing about it. But I learnt more later, especially after becoming a Christian in my early twenties, as Linda had done. It helped that I had a Jewish believer as my early mentor, and I became increasingly aware of the significance of our Jewish heritage, about which I now write prolifically. Meanwhile Linda, who has been teaching Christianity in Doncaster area schools for over 30 years, also now teaches about Judaism as it forms the context into which Christ came to us, fulfilling all the laws and promises of the Old Testament. So in both our cases, we were kept in the dark about very important aspects of our lives – until the Lord shone his light on the truth. Which brings me to the Christian Church as a whole, especially in the UK. We have known very little, if anything, of our faith’s Jewish roots or of God’s ongoing purposes for Israel. This needs to change – and fast! For we are surely hurtling towards the Messiah’s Second Coming like a high-speed train, in danger of coming off the rails with the rest of humanity if we fail to get to grips with how we Christians fit into the unfolding picture of global opposition to tiny Israel. What is our role as we watch antisemitism spread across the globe like wildfire? Do we just sit and watch, or write it off as having nothing to do with us, and remain silent? Or do we stand up to be counted as those who refuse to salute the new Nazism that portrays itself as anti-Zionism – a Confessing Church walking the way of the cross for God’s chosen people? My questions come as renewed calls are made for an independent inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC following news that Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon has won £400,000 in compensation from the broadcaster. Lucie’s career is said to have unravelled after she raised concerns about antisemitism within the BBC, though the latter have not admitted to any fault. This is highly significant as millions of UK Christians are (where Israel is concerned) probably more influenced by what they hear from our national broadcaster than what they read in the Bible.
